questions.stem:
Three-address code is evaluated line by line. What does this program print?

```python
a, b, c = 2, 3, 4
t1 = a * b
t2 = t1 + c
x = t2 - a
print(x)
```

This pseudo-code uses labels and jumps. What value of s is printed?

```text
i = 1
s = 0
L:  if i > 4 goto END
    s = s + i
    i = i + 1
    goto L
END: print(s)
```
questions.explain: The jump back to L makes a loop that adds i = 1, 2, 3 and 4 to s. When i reaches 5 the test jumps to END, so s = 10.

questions.stem: In the parse tree of `3 + 4 * 2` for the usual expression grammar, the multiplication node sits below the addition node. Each node computes its value from its children. What value does the root get?
questions.explain: The multiplication node gives 4 × 2 = 8 first. The root then adds 3 + 8 = 11.

questions.stem: main calls f, f calls g, and g calls h. While h is running, how many activation records (stack frames) are on the call stack, counting main?
questions.explain: Each active call has its own record: main, f, g and h. That is 4.

questions.stem: One pass over a program with n basic blocks costs O(n). If the pass is repeated up to n times, what is the worst-case total cost?
questions.explain: n repetitions of an O(n) pass cost n × n = n².
